messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Procedure for Handling Dual Refactors
parts:
Right now there are two big, concurrent refactors:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/tree/feature/issue-1361-writer_callback

Substantial refactor of the API into services and interface callbacks,
implementing a writer callback to remove any system I/O dependencies.

and

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/tree/feature/refactor_io_reader_writer

Refactors var_context, eventually will clean up the
generated model code and completely template out
most of the services.

Already there have been merges that will conflict with these refactors,
but my main concern right now is whether to try to keep these
refactors together or not. Propagating changes to the var_context
implementations will require changing command/services which
would have to be rewritten unless the first branch is merged first.

I see a few possible means of moving forward:

1) Keep these separate branches independent of each other and
just swallow a nasty merge process down the line.

2) Merge the writer_callback after 2.7.

3) Create a Stan3 branch, merge the writer callback into that
and then work the var_context refactor off of this new Stan3
branch.

How should we do this? Either way there’s going to be a few
big merges that we’ll have to muck through given how much code
is getting changed.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Procedure for Handling Dual Refactors
parts:
All else being equal, we want small pull requests.

So I'd recommend doing one first rather than working
in parallel, so that merge is less nasty. I think
that's your option (2).

All else not being equal, it's not the end of the world
if you put them together to save your sanity.

- Bob

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Procedure for Handling Dual Refactors
parts:
I'd suggest making conceptually smaller branches. Then it's easy enough to daisy chain the branches.

For example, if you wanted to add tests for scaffolding, do that on a branch first, and get that a stand-alone pull request. If you find a problem with some portion of the code and want to change it, instead of rolling it into a larger pull request, get that on a separate one and merge that into your branch and get the pull request going.

For the writer_callback branch, I really want to break it into a handful of pull requests. I've just been wrestling with the math library, so I haven't had the chance to do it myself.


Daniel

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Procedure for Handling Dual Refactors
parts:
There is no easy way to break these into smaller pull requests —
the changes are too interconnected.  If someone wants to try to
do that, fine, but I think that it’s a complete waste of time.  Once
we have working refactors in we can add tests and such in waves
of smaller commits.

And this doesn’t even consider the interfaces.

Basically I do not want these refactors to wait for other things —
if that means having a Stan3 branch that incorporates all of the
refactors (and eventually argument changes) while the interfaces
work off of 2.7+ fine.
